text:
PagerDuty: INC-2026-448 triggered - gateway error rate spike on /v1/generate, 5xx ~= 18% over last 5m (baseline ~0.5%). Paging on-call now. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: alert details: rule=gateway.error_rate; scope=us-west; top error=gateway_timeout, downstream=kv-prefix-cache.
Devon: I'm on-call, ack. Starting collection: grabbing gateway logs + kv cache metrics. Anyone seen anything similar earlier?
Carla: I see a correlated bump in kv-prefix-cache miss rate and a sharp drop in cache hit ratio at 12:28 UTC. Also seeing repeated checksum validation failures from the cache reader: `checksum_mismatch` entries.
Iman: forwarding relevant log snippet: ```
[2026-03-14T12:27:56Z] kv-prefix-cache shard=17 prefix=rdx/abcd checksum=0x9f3a expected=0x4b21 error=checksum_mismatch
[2026-03-14T12:27:57Z] kv-prefix-cache shard=17 prefix=rdx/abcd evict_reason=ttl_zero frequency=512
[2026-03-14T12:28:01Z] gateway handler=rewrite cache_read=failed fallback=direct_request elapsed=1.2s status=504
```
Lucas: interesting — `evict_reason=ttl_zero frequency=512` suggests mass invalidation on that shard. Metric histograms show a huge spike in `cache.evicts_per_second` starting 12:26. Could be a TTL regression or a compaction job triggering invalidations.
Devon: can we confirm if a new rolling config hit cache service around that time? deploy logs?
SRE-Bot: deploy-bot: `release/kv-cache@v2.14.0` rollout completed to 60% at 12:24, 100% at 12:29 in us-west. Trigger: auto-rollout from config change `cache.default_ttl` set to `0s` by mistake in infra/cfg.
Devon: oh. that would explain ttl_zero. Rolling config that set TTL to 0 essentially made entries immediately evict -> avalanche of misses -> overload downstream storage -> gateway timeouts.
Carla: mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout and rollback config to previous TTL 1h, 2) enable cache read-only fallback (serve stale) for gateway, 3) scale kv-cache replicas temporarily to absorb misses. I'll take 1 and 2.
Iman: running rollback now: `kubectl set env deployment/kv-cache CACHE_DEFAULT_TTL=1h -n infra` and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -n infra --timeout=0s` (doing canary first).
Devon: I'll enable stale-serve fallback on gateway: `gateway.config.cache_strategies.fallback=serve_stale` and push via feature toggle. Applying to us-west canary.
Alex: I'm scaling cache replicas: `k scale deployment/kv-cache --replicas=8 -n infra` (from 3->8). Also opening a quick patch to add backpressure limit on cache write path so origin won't overload backends.
Support-Bot: creating CS/ops ticket for customers impacted. Early estimate: ~7% of production requests hit 5xx/timeout during the spike window 12:26-12:45. Noting top affected customers on Dedicated plans.
SRE-Bot: health checks: cache hit ratio recovering after rollback applied to 20% at 12:34. Full rollback completed at 12:38. Hit ratio trending toward baseline by 12:46. 5xx rate dropping to ~1.2% at 12:50.
Devon: good. What about corrupted entries/checksums? Are they just symptoms from TTL eviction or actual data corruption?
Iman: logs show checksum_mismatch mostly on recently evicted prefixes; hypothesis: the TTL=0 forced entries out while background compactor was reading, leaving partial entries -> checksum mismatch on read. No evidence of persistent corruption on disk. Running `kv-check` across affected shard set to verify.
Lucas: adding a compensating safety: we'll introduce a short grace-window on the cache read path to tolerate checksum mismatch and fallback to origin rather than throw upstream 5xx. Patch queued: `cache.read.on_checksum_mismatch = fallback_origin` (hotfix).
Carla: live patch applied to canary at 12:41. Monitoring.
Devon: any customer-facing comms drafted? Alex, Support?
Alex: Support drafted a status update: "We experienced elevated errors for inference requests in us-west due to a configuration rollback issue with our prefix cache. The issue has been mitigated and full service restored. We're following up with a postmortem and remediation plan." Sending to CS for review.
Support-Bot: CS/ops ticket updated with impacted customers list and suggested credit amounts.
Devon: handoff plan — I'm going offline 13:00 UTC. Alex will take primary on-call for follow-through and postmortem. Alex, you good to take over?
Alex: taking over.)
